sources.title: Model Card for Aya Vision 32B
sources.evidence: Names the exact model, developer, open-weight research release, nominal 32-billion size, 16K context, text/image inputs and text output. Describes OCR, captioning, visual reasoning and question answering. Links the noncommercial license and Aya Expanse 32B backbone. The card body is readable, although checkpoint downloads require access approval and authentication. Reopened on 2026-10-27: the card still names Aya Expanse 32B as the language backbone, advertises nominal 32B and specifies SigLIP2-patch14-384; no active count is stated.

sources.title: Aya Vision API documentation
sources.evidence: The exact c4ai-aya-vision-32b row specifies nominal 32 billion parameters, text/image modality, 16k context and 4k maximum output. Documents captioning, visual question answering, text generation and translation, and downloadable research weights. Reopened on 2026-10-27; the nominal 32B row remains, without an active-parameter count.

sources.title: Our Groundbreaking Multimodal Model, Aya Vision, is Here!
sources.evidence: The March 4, 2025 release note announces Aya Vision that day and identifies Cohere Labs as Cohere's research arm.

sources.title: Aya Vision: Expanding the worlds AI can see
sources.evidence: Dated March 4, 2025. The page's embedded article text explicitly releases both 8B and 32B weights and says they are available that day; the web text extractor exposed only the article heading, so the embedded article was also inspected directly.

sources.title: Aya Vision: Advancing the Frontier of Multilingual Multimodality
sources.evidence: May 13, 2025 report, section 4.1 and Table 6: the 32B variant combines Aya Expanse 32B, a SigLIP2-so400m-patch16-512 encoder and a SwiGLU connector. Nominal component counts are 32.3B LLM, 400M encoder and 428M connector. The LLM has 40 layers, 8192 width, 64 query heads and 8 KV heads. It calls Aya Vision a model family. Independently inspected sections 4.1-4.2 and Appendix B Table 6 in the full official report fetched on 2026-10-27, and searched its complete text for active-parameter disclosures. The three component counts sum to 33.128B before rounding. Cross-modal merging retains the language-model architecture; neither Table 6 nor the reviewed report states an active-parameter count.

sources.title: Public metadata for the original Aya Vision 32B checkpoint
sources.publisher: Hugging Face metadata for Cohere Labs repository
sources.evidence: Public metadata declares AyaVisionForConditionalGeneration, automatic gating, 15 safetensors shards and 33,137,896,688 F16 tensor elements. This aggregate is not an independently inspected learned-parameter count. No shard headers were accessible. The repository creation timestamp is March 2, 2025, which is not used as the public release date. Reopened the public metadata API on 2026-10-27: total remains 33,137,896,688 F16 elements and the repository remains automatically gated. No new weight or shard-header requests were made.

sources.title: Original checkpoint configuration access attempt
sources.evidence: Unauthenticated raw/main and resolve/main config requests returned HTTP 401 with an access-restricted/authentication-required message. Retained evidence from the original 2026-10-26 audit; not retried in the parameter re-audit.

sources.title: Original safetensors index access attempt
sources.evidence: Unauthenticated request returned HTTP 401. Index contents and the complete tensor name inventory could not be inspected. Retained evidence from the original 2026-10-26 audit; not retried in the parameter re-audit.

sources.title: Original safetensors header access attempt
sources.evidence: An unauthenticated Range: bytes=0-7 request returned HTTP 401. No weight shard was downloaded; buffer exclusion and exact learned-parameter counting remain unverified. Retained evidence from the original 2026-10-26 audit; not retried in the parameter re-audit.

sources.title: Aya Expanse 32B backbone model card
sources.evidence: Describes the specifically identified language backbone as an autoregressive language model using an optimized Transformer architecture. Backbone evidence is used for structure, not to transfer its context limit or capabilities to Aya Vision. Reopened on 2026-10-27: the named backbone card documents supervised finetuning, preference training and model merging, but does not publish an active-count convention.

sources.title: Cohere Aya Vision implementation in the model card's recommended Transformers revision
sources.publisher: Cohere Inc. team / Hugging Face Transformers
sources.evidence: The Cohere-authored implementation constructs a vision tower, dense two-linear-layer multimodal projector and a causal language model. It confirms the late-fusion structure and processes the vision tower only when image inputs are present. Reopened on 2026-10-27: forward processes image features only when pixel_values is present, and cached decoding omits the image path. This distinguishes image encoding from language decoding but does not define a numerical active-parameter convention.

sources.title: Cohere decoder implementation in the Aya Vision release revision
sources.evidence: CohereDecoderLayer combines attention and a CohereMLP with ordinary gate/up/down linear projections; it does not route tokens among experts. This corroborates a dense Transformer classification for the documented Aya Expanse backbone.

sources.title: CC-BY-NC 4.0 License with Acceptable Use Addendum
sources.evidence: The license linked by the model card is Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 with a Cohere Labs acceptable-use addendum.

sources.title: Reasoning Capabilities
sources.evidence: Documents dedicated thinking blocks and the Command A Reasoning endpoint. It does not give an explicit reasoning-mode support decision for Aya Vision 32B.

sources.title: Basic usage of tool use (function calling)
sources.evidence: Introduces native tool use for the Command family. It does not explicitly establish support or lack of support for Aya Vision 32B.

sources.title: Aya Expanse: Combining Research Breakthroughs for a New Multilingual Frontier
sources.evidence: Searched the complete official report fetched on 2026-10-27 and independently inspected the Aya Expanse 32B lineage and parameter passages. It gives the nominal 32B size and post-training/model-merging recipe. Its explicit 39B active-parameter count describes the comparison model Mixtral-8x22B (141B total), not Aya Expanse. It supplies no active count to inherit for the Aya Vision 32B language backbone.

sources.title: Tiny Aya technical report
sources.evidence: Searched the complete later first-party report fetched on 2026-10-27 and independently inspected section 3.1 and Table 2. The table labels Tiny Aya counts as 0.5B embedding, 2.8B non-embedding and 3.35B total. These are not active-count labels and concern a different architecture/checkpoint; no Aya Vision or Aya Expanse active count is established.

sources.title: Command A: An Enterprise-Ready Large Language Model
sources.evidence: Searched the complete first-party v2 report fetched on 2026-10-27 and independently inspected architecture section 2.3 and the model comparisons. The 111B statement concerns Command A, and neither its comparisons nor its dense architecture discussion publishes an active count for Aya Vision 32B or Aya Expanse 32B.

sources.title: Introducing Command A+
sources.evidence: Reopened the later first-party release and comparison table on 2026-10-27. It gives 218B total and 25B active for the distinct Command A+ MoE and lists Command A-family sizes of 111B/112B. Aya Vision and Aya Expanse are absent from the comparison; these newer counts cannot be transferred to Aya Vision 32B.

developer.note: Cohere Labs is the named development team within Cohere; retain the catalog's company-level developer.

family.note: Normalized family key for the explicitly named Aya Vision family.

release_date.note: Explicit public launch and availability date; not repository creation or later paper submission.

open_weights.note: Research weights are distributed under noncommercial terms; gated access does not negate their release.

license.note: Retain the named license; the additional acceptable-use condition is recorded in notes.

parameters_b.note: Retain approximately 33.1B complete multimodal parameters: the developer report gives 32.3B language model + 0.4B vision encoder + 0.428B connector = 33.128B before rounding. This includes the learned encoder even when frozen during training. It is a sum of nominal component counts, not an exact tensor census; the public 33,137,896,688-element metadata remains corroboration only. Prior gated-file and encoder-variant limitations remain recorded in the source evidence.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh exact-model total/active and named-backbone searches, reopened cards/implementation, and later Cohere report/comparison checks found no published active-count convention for Aya Vision 32B or its Aya Expanse 32B backbone. The implementation separates image encoding from cached language decoding, so complete multimodal total cannot stand in for per-token active parameters. The documented 32.3B is a language-model total, not a supported active count. Do not transfer Mixtral/Command A+ active counts or Tiny Aya non-embedding counts.

architecture.note: Classification inferred from the documented Transformer backbone and ordinary dense implementation, with a vision encoder and MLP connector. Exact-variant conflict: the paper specifies patch16-512, while the current card specifies patch14-384; inaccessible checkpoint config prevents adjudication.

context_window.note: Retains the documented nominal 16k context in decimal catalog units; an exact 16,384-token implementation limit was not established.

modalities.note: Explicit input/output descriptions and API examples agree.

reasoning.note: Visual reasoning capability is documented, but dedicated reasoning/thinking mode support is not. Neither true nor the baseline false is established.

tool_call.note: Reviewed card, public chat template and tool-use documentation do not provide an exact-model native function-calling support statement. Clear unsupported false.

description.value: Open multilingual vision model for OCR, visual reasoning, and image question answering
description.note: The stated capabilities are explicitly supported; no benchmark superiority claim is added.

patch.notes: Approximately 33.1B total: 32.3B language model, 0.4B vision encoder and 0.428B connector, from the developer's rounded component counts. Active parameters are not separately disclosed for either the complete model or its language backbone. The paper's patch16-512 encoder conflicts with the model card's patch14-384 description. The CC-BY-NC-4.0 release also requires Cohere Labs' acceptable-use addendum. Dedicated reasoning-mode and native tool-calling flags remain unverified.

summary: Parameter re-audit on 2026-10-27 retained the approximate 33.1B complete multimodal total and component breakdown. Reopened exact-model and backbone evidence, reran total/active/lineage searches, and checked the full Aya Vision, Aya Expanse, Tiny Aya and Command A reports plus the later Command A+ comparison. No supported complete-model or language-only active count was found; active remains explicitly null. Preserved prior metadata/census limitations and all unrelated assessments; no weight shards requested.
